quote: The current study tracked 183 students applying for full‐time, paid jobs in their field, in connection with a postsecondary co‐operative education program in Canada.
rationale: The study is an observational tracking of job applicants' resumes and cover letters. Students do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. ChatGPT is mentioned only as speculation. The content is not STEM learning and the outcome is hiring success, not learning. The first applicable code is E1.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey with regression; no control group without generative AI, no intervention, and the outcome is a disposition (affective/self-report), not a learning measure. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group).

quote: A quantitative, descriptive, and exploratory approach was adopted with data collected through a structured questionnaire distributed via Google Forms.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of student perceptions. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and no experimental or quasi-experimental design. The protocol's order of codes puts E1 first, but the abstract does not say that learners used a generative AI tool in a learning activity (65% had never used ChatGPT). The clearest failure is the absence of a control group without generative AI, so I used E3. E5 would also apply, because only perceptions were measured.

quote: Making Generative AI Use Visible in a Foundational Health-Sciences Course: Effects on Learning, Verification and Attribution
rationale: No abstract is available. The title points to generative AI and a learning outcome, but it also suggests health-sciences content that may count as excluded health professions education. The title does not show whether the course is health professions training, so the domain is not clearly failed. The comparison group, design, and data are also unknown. I am advancing this record to full text instead of excluding it on missing information.

quote: We employed a novel combination of manual and AI-assisted thematic coding to analyse students' reflective writings using CPM.
rationale: Generative AI was used by researchers as an analysis tool for coding students' reflections, not as a learner-facing learning tool. There is no control group and no learning outcome, only emotion analysis. E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: A structured questionnaire was administered to 299 university students during the 2026-1 academic period.
rationale: This is a survey study. It builds classification models to predict perceived cognitive dependence. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM domain focus. The design is correlational and the outcome is perceptual. The protocol's code order puts E1 first, but the abstract describes no learning-activity intervention and no comparison group. E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the clearest code, and every code from E1 to E5 would fail.

quote: involving a total of 617 university students enrolled in art programs
rationale: The content is art and creativity, which is not STEM. The study also looks like a survey with network analysis, and it reports no learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This paper proposes an AI-Enabled Pedagogical Framework for integrating Indian Knowledge Systems into teacher education.
rationale: The paper proposes a conceptual framework and a prototype, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. The content, Indian Knowledge Systems in teacher education, is also not clearly STEM. The abstract gives positive evidence that it is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion codes are reported in order, but E1–E5 are not clearly established from the abstract alone.

quote: compares the accuracy of grades suggested by the GPT-4 model with those awarded by university teachers
rationale: GPT-4 is used only to grade essays, not as a learner-facing tool. The protocol excludes AI used only for grading. The content is political science, which is not STEM, and there is no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: Learner autonomy driven by (generative) artificial intelligence as a source of emotional vulnerability and identity tensions in mid-career tertiary-level language teachers
rationale: No abstract is available, so the decision rests on the title. The title shows the content is language teaching, which is non-STEM. The participants are mid-career language teachers, who are in-service rather than students. The outcomes are emotional vulnerability and identity tensions, not a learning measure. Several criteria fail on the title alone. E2 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: A comprehensive analysis of the literature on the subject was conducted by the authors, who consider 66 papers that were found in the Scopus database.
rationale: This is a literature review with bibliometric analysis of many technologies in accounting education. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool in it, so E1 applies, and E1 comes first in the exclusion order. It would also fail on other criteria: accounting is not STEM (E2), and it is not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome (E6, E3, E5).

quote: This book, comprising twenty-six chapters, delves deep into the multifaceted realm of AI-driven STEM education.
rationale: The record is an edited book that surveys AI in STEM education. It is not an empirical study. It reports no specific intervention, no control group and no learning outcome data. It is also not a journal article. E6 is the best-fitting code.

quote: this study extends prior educational designs by integrating unsupervised learning components into an experiential physical computing kit, enabling learners to engage with feature extraction and clustering processes
rationale: The intervention is a physical computing kit (robots) for teaching supervised and unsupervised learning. Generative AI is mentioned only as background, and learners do not interact with a generative AI tool. The abstract describes tool development with no evaluation, so E1 applies first. The venue (AHFE International) also suggests conference proceedings, but E1 comes earlier in the code order.

quote: to investigate the effectiveness and applicability of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Agent in assessing intermediate-level Chinese writing produced by learners of Chinese as a second language (L2)
rationale: The AI agent is used only to grade essays, so it is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The content is also Chinese language learning, which is not STEM. The design compares AI scores with teacher scores, with no control group. E1 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: Training and assistance in the creation of scientific articles based on artificial intelligence (AI) aims to improve the scientific writing skills of prospective teachers
rationale: The learning target is scientific article writing, grammar and reference management, which is not STEM content (E2 comes first in the code order). The record also seems to describe a single 25-person training group with no control group, which would fail E3 and the design criterion. It reads as a community service program rather than a controlled study.

quote: this study investigated how college students engaged with the feedback provided by ChatGPT on their International English Language Testing System writing tasks. Sixteen undergraduates voluntarily participated in unobtrusive observations and stimulated recall interviews.
rationale: Content is English writing (IELTS), which is not STEM. The study is also qualitative (observations and interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: Keyword Index Venue: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association
rationale: The record is a keyword index of a medical journal, not an empirical study. It describes no generative AI learning intervention, STEM learning, or learning outcome. The listed medical terms, such as "Artificial intelligence 87:259", are only index entries. E6 (not an empirical study) fits best.

quote: We adopted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design. First, a survey with 56 undergraduate computing students at the University of Brasília (UnB) examined familiarity with 21 AI ethical principles
rationale: The study is a survey and interview study of ethical literacy and educator perceptions. No learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the intervention criterion first (E1). It also fails on comparison, design and outcome.

quote: This study investigates the awareness and perceptions of ChatGPT among a sample of 300 students and 50 teachers at Sharda University, employing the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT)
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of awareness and perceptions analysed with descriptive statistics and ANOVA across demographic groups. It has no control group without generative AI and no learning outcome. This is a survey design, so it fails the comparison, design and outcome criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Data from 938 undergraduates, merged with administrative records, revealed disparities in ChatGPT awareness and use
rationale: This is a survey study of student awareness and use of ChatGPT. It has no control group and no learning outcome. Under the ordered exclusion codes, the first failing criterion is the comparison (E3), because there is no non-generative-AI control group. The design is also survey/correlational and the outcomes are usage only.

quote: Analysis of the capabilities of generative artificial intelligence for generating individual teaching materials (using the example of the disciplines Programming and Foreign (English) language.

quote: Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the study involved ten students from the Arabic Language Education Program as research participants.
rationale: The content is Arabic writing skills, which is language learning and not STEM. The study is also descriptive qualitative, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order. The abstract names ChatGPT and Gemini, so E1 does not apply.

quote: Nursing students’ perceptions and ethical considerations of ChatGPT usage in nursing education: A cross-sectional study
rationale: No abstract is available, but the title gives positive evidence of exclusion. The content is nursing education, which is health professions and not STEM. The design is cross-sectional and the focus is perceptions, so there is likely no control group and no learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: We compare two strategies, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Continual Pre-Training (CPT), to extend LLMs with course-specific knowledge.

quote: Regression analysis shows that frequent use of ChatGPT is a predictor for reduced FLA alongside perceived usefulness, ease of use, and positive attitudes towards the tool.

quote: The author of the presentation contends that the future of higher education lies in collaborative originality.

quote: the study draws on semi-structured interviews and AI policy documents from writing programs to explore how identity, ideology, and power intersect in writing classrooms
rationale: Qualitative interview study of five graduate teaching assistants about their identities in college writing classrooms. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the content is writing (non-STEM). E1 is the first code in order that applies, since the study does not test a learner-facing generative AI intervention.

quote: Thirty of these problems were submitted to ChatGPT-3.5. For the remaining 10 problems, we retrieved past minimally passing student responses. Six tutors graded each of the 40 responses.

rationale: The study benchmarks ChatGPT's responses to assessment prompts. The first applicable code in order is E1, because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: This study investigates the use of ChatGPT and media-based collaborative learning to enhance metapragmatic awareness among 30 Korean EFL university students.

quote: ChatGPT applied the framework to categorize each course, with human coders independently validating a subset of the assessments to ensure reliability.
rationale: ChatGPT was used by researchers to analyze course outlines, not by learners in a learning activity. There is no learner-facing generative AI, no control group and no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code.

rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT) is used by educators to create tests, so it is not learner-facing. The only experiment reported is about speed of test generation, not student learning. Per the protocol, AI used only by the teacher is E1.

quote: Nowadays, the need for ever more sophisticated data processing makes it even harder to meet the open data standards, which are needed going forward to make data accessible and synoptic analyses possible
rationale: The record is an opinion or commentary piece on publishing ocean datasets and using AI for metadata. It describes no learners, no learner-facing generative AI, no control group and no learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1, because the AI is a researcher-side data tool and not learner-facing. It is also not an empirical study, which would be E6.

quote: we curate a new QG dataset called EduProbe for school-level subjects, by leveraging the rich content of NCERT textbooks.
rationale: The study builds a question-generation dataset and benchmarks LLMs with automatic and human evaluation of the generated questions. No learners interact with a generative AI tool, and there is no learning outcome or control group. The first applicable exclusion code is E1, because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: developing intercultural competence among linguistics students
rationale: The content is intercultural competence in linguistics and foreign language teaching. This is non-STEM (language learning), so it fails the domain criterion.

quote: This paper presents insights from "The Fifth Biomedical Engineering Education Summit", which brought together educators from across the U.S.
rationale: The record reports summit discussions and recommendations in a question-response format. It is not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learning outcome and no experimental design, so E6 applies.

quote: Using a quantitative survey-based methodology, data were collected from 320 undergraduate and postgraduate students at a Sri Lankan university
rationale: The study is a correlational survey of perceptions with no control group without generative AI. It measures perceived learning outcomes only, and the domain is not STEM-specific. The design fails the protocol. By the ordered exclusion codes, E3 (no control group) is the first that clearly applies. E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract.

quote: This research employs a qualitative, multi-stage approach. First, a comprehensive literature review was conducted to analyze and synthesize the theoretical conception and multi-dimensional structure of prompt literacy.
rationale: The study is a qualitative conceptual and framework paper based on a literature review. It has no empirical learner intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is about public prompt literacy in libraries, not STEM learning. Several codes could apply. E6 (not an empirical study) is the most fitting, and it is reasonable to apply it before E2 and E3 in this case. Strictly, E2 is listed before E6 in the code order, and non-STEM content is also clear. E2 would therefore be the first applicable code by order.

quote: The article methodically explores the potential for using webquest technology as an innovative means for professionally-oriented foreign language teaching in higher education institutions
rationale: The intervention is webquest technology on Moodle, not a learner-facing generative AI tool. Generative AI appears only as a future prospect. The content is foreign language teaching, which is also non-STEM, and the article is a methodological description with no control group. E1 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: Psychometric Properties and Assessment of Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice Towards ChatGPT in Pharmacy Practice and Education: a Study Protocol
rationale: No abstract is available, but the title gives positive evidence of failure. The domain is pharmacy, which is health professions education and is excluded. The record is also a study protocol for a knowledge-attitude-practice survey, so it has no comparison group and no learning outcome. The domain is the first applicable exclusion code in the protocol order.

quote: This paper provides a glimpse of the status quo of generative (Gen) AI in contexts where English is not used natively.
rationale: The record is about English language learning and teaching, which is non-STEM. The protocol excludes language learning. The paper is also a discussion or review, not an empirical study. E2 comes first in the code order, so I used E2.

quote: It was applied in a team-based project involving 15 university students. To examine its effectiveness, the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT-Figural) were conducted before and after the intervention
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 15 students measured before and after the intervention, with no separate control group without generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol codes as E3. The domain (creativity and design thinking) is also doubtfully STEM, but the missing control group is enough to exclude.

quote: we introduce Claude-Light, a lightweight, remotely accessible instrument designed for prototyping automation algorithms and machine learning workflows.
rationale: The abstract describes a instrument and demonstrates its use, with a discussion of LLMs in lab automation. It reports no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome. This is a descriptive or tool paper. The criteria are not met, so the first applicable code in order is E3. E6 (not empirical) would also fit, but E3 comes first in the order. Because the evidence is positive, I am excluding at the abstract stage.

quote: Mathematical Biology (The MIT Press, 2025), by Markus Meister (Caltech), Kyu Hyun Lee (UCSF), and Ruben Portugues (Technical University of Munich), covers the principles and applications of linear algebra, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems.
rationale: This is a book review column that describes several books. It is not an empirical study. It has no intervention, no comparison group and no learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence that it fails the empirical design criteria.

quote: fashion marketing education by integrating generative artificial intelligence (AI) within a problem-based learning (PBL) framework
rationale: Content is fashion marketing, which is not a STEM domain. E2 is the first applicable code in order. The study also appears to be a single-group pre-post design with no control group.

quote: Extended Talk Abstract
rationale: The record is an extended talk abstract at a workshop (DataEd@SIGMOD). It is a conference-type record, not a journal article. It is also not an empirical study of learner-facing generative AI. It describes non-generative query-debugging systems and future work. Under the code order, E1 and E6 might also apply. The publication type is the clearest positive evidence, so I used E10. This follows the borderline rule that conference papers and work in progress that reach screening get E10.

quote: data were collected through a questionnaire of 24 items across six factors on a 5-point Likert scale. Using multiple linear regression analysis with RStudio
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of behavioural intention (UTAUT) with regression. It has no control group and no learning outcome. By the ordered codes, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first that applies, since the record is empirical and the intervention is not clearly learner-facing. The design and outcome criteria also fail.

quote: An anonymous online survey was conducted among 402 students in grades 6-11 of general secondary education institutions in Lviv Region during 2025-2026.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of children's trust in health information sources. There is no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, no STEM domain, and no learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1, because AI agents appear only as a trust-rated source and not as a learning activity.

quote: an empirical analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). A multi-stage stratified sampling method was adopted, with a sample of 842 college students
rationale: This is a cross-sectional survey study using PLS-SEM on adoption intention (TAM/UTAUT2). It has no control group, no learning intervention and no learning outcome. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design. By the ordered exclusion codes, E1 might come first, since there is no learner-facing intervention. However, the abstract describes survey-based adoption intention, and the closest code on the comparison/design failure is E3. The comparison and design criteria clearly fail, and the outcome is only perceptions, so it is excluded.

quote: Pictured on qualitative methodology, semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven participants—five university students and two ESL instructors from Pakistani public sector universities.
rationale: The content is ESL (language learning), which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. The design is also qualitative interviews with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the code order, E2 is the first exclusion code that applies. E1 is not assigned because the abstract only mentions AI tools in passing, and that is not positive evidence of a failed intervention criterion.

quote: The performance of Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro, GPT-4o, and 48 students was compared using 80 OSPDE questions
rationale: The study benchmarks AI models answering exam questions against a retrospective student cohort. Students do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The domain is dental education, which is health professions and so non-STEM. The abstract gives positive evidence of failure on intervention. E1 is first in the code order.

quote: Вплив діджиталізації на спектр вмінь англомовної компетентності студентів закладів вищої освіти в рамках професійної підготовки
rationale: The title shows the content is English-language competence of higher-education students, which is language learning and so not STEM. The repository venue also suggests it is not a journal article.

quote: we synthesise current LLM-based study support with earlier traditions in artificial intelligence in education to develop a contemporary account of AI learning companions
rationale: The paper is a conceptual synthesis and design framework. It applies the framework to five illustrative case studies. The abstract reports no controlled experiment, no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies.

quote: The program focuses on training teachers in prompt engineering as a foundational skill for using generative AI to develop teaching materials and assessments.
rationale: This is a teacher training workshop. Teachers use generative AI to prepare materials, so students do not interact with it. The intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The abstract also shows no control group, no STEM focus, and a teacher population.

quote: A post-course survey, combining quantitative items and open-ended responses, was analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic synthesis.
rationale: Single-group pilot of 16 master's students with only a post-course survey; no separate non-GenAI control group, and outcomes are perceptions/satisfaction rather than a learning measure. Design is survey-based. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group).

quote: This paper explores the feasibility of integrating large language models (DeepSeek) into the teaching of Signals and Systems.
rationale: Abstract describes LLM use in a STEM higher-education course, but it reports no control group, design, or quantitative learning outcome. The "teaching case" wording suggests a descriptive or design paper, but that is not positive evidence of failure. Missing information is not grounds for exclusion at abstract stage, so resolve at full text. The Chinese/English abstract is not a reason to exclude at this stage.

quote: This paper presents a framework consisting of open, executable module library that lowers the entry barrier for AI in power systems.
rationale: The paper presents a teaching module library about AI (DNN, CNN, DRL, PINN) for power systems. Learners are not shown interacting with a generative AI tool. The abstract reports only a survey, webinar attendance and repository visits, with no control group and no learning outcome. The intervention criterion clearly fails, so E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study provides a comprehensive quantitative benchmark of the ChatGPT-4 model’s performance on the Fundamentals of Engineering (FE) Civil Exam.
rationale: The study is a benchmark of ChatGPT-4 answering exam questions, run by the researchers. No students interact with the AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). It also has no student participants, no control group and no learning outcome, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Data from an anonymous survey collected at an Australian university (n = 126) are analysed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) approach.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey analysed with PLS-SEM. There is no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome. Intention and reliance are not learning measures. The first applicable code in order is E3, because no control group without generative AI exists. E5 also applies but comes later in the order.

quote: This study examines the impact of GenAI-enabled SRL assistance for self-regulated reading strategies and engagement of university-level EFL students
rationale: The content is EFL reading, which is language learning and not STEM, so the domain exclusion applies. The outcomes are self-regulation strategies and engagement, which are affective or behavioural and not STEM learning. The intervention (GenAI chatbot), the quasi-experimental design with a control group, and the university population would otherwise be acceptable.

quote: This conversation with ChatGPT, and associated critical evaluation, provides an insight into the capabilities and limitations of LLMs and informs on the possibilities for incorporating AI into bioscience education
rationale: The paper is a conversation with ChatGPT and a critical commentary. It is not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner intervention and no quantitative learning outcome. Because it is not empirical, E6 applies first in the code order that fits, and the bioscience domain is a secondary concern.

quote: Literacy as a Technology: a Conversation with Kyle Jensen about AI, Writing and More

quote: Several suggestions are given for how instructors can pivot to focus on the problem-solving process and research-based activities that engage students in learning without sacrificing rigor.

rationale: The venue is a conference (International Convention on ICT, Electronics and Microelectronics), so the record is conference proceedings and E10 applies. quote: I would like to share my experience on how the pandemic irreversibly accelerated the use of digital tools
rationale: The record is a personal reflection or experience narrative on digital tools in Analytical Chemistry teaching during the pandemic. quote: A mixed-methods approach was employed to collect quantitative and qualitative data from 282 students. Quantitative data were analysed through descriptive and K-means clustering, while the open-ended question was thematically coded.

E3 comes first in the stated order only if the intervention is judged met, so the choice between E1 and E3 is borderline. quote: the research employed descriptive with qualitative support. Quantitative data were gathered through surveys administered to Bachelor of Secondary Education major in English students
rationale: The content is academic English writing, which is non-STEM, so E2 is the first code that applies. The study is also a descriptive survey and interview study of perceptions. It has no control group and no learning outcome, so it would fail on those criteria as well.

quote: Using a framework-based content analysis, student projects across science and technology, and business domains were examined to assess AI integration and the development of competencies
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of student projects from one challenge. It has no separate control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. E3 is the first applicable code in the order.

quote: through the analysis of interview data from 30 undergraduate medical students
rationale: Qualitative grounded theory interview study on willingness to use ChatGPT. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). The design and outcome criteria also fail. quote: An exploratory-descriptive mixed-methods design was adopted. Data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to 28 participants (9 teacher trainers and 19 trainee teachers)
rationale: The content is English language teaching, which is non-STEM, so E2 is the first code that applies. The study is also a descriptive questionnaire survey of perceptions. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure.

quote: this paper analyzes the internal mechanism of AIempowered interdisciplinary PBL in Emerging Engineering Education from the perspectives of policy logic, technical logic, and knowledge logic. It further proposes a teaching resource system
